title: XML in Diamond Open Access Journal Publishing

creators.name: Jertec Musap, Ljiljana
creators.affiliation: SRCE – University of Zagreb University Computing Centre

description:
Archive and open educational resources of the online course XML Publishing, published on the EDCH Training platform (European Diamond Capacity Hub). The course introduces XML and its use in scholarly publishing, with a focus on Diamond Open Access journals, JATS XML and XML-based publishing workflows in OJS. It was developed within the CRAFT-OA project (2023–2025).

Learning outcomes — after the course, learners can:

  • explain what XML and its standards are and why they matter for publishing;
  • explain why XML is essential for data exchange, visualisation and quality;
  • structure JATS articles for optimal discoverability;
  • convert DOCX files using the JATS XML Converter Service;
  • implement XML workflows using OJS plugins.

Audience: {{TO_COMPLETE: audience}}
Level: {{TO_COMPLETE: level}}
Prerequisites: {{TO_COMPLETE: prerequisites}}
Format: self-paced online course, 9 modules, about 90 minutes. Language: English.

Contents: the Moodle course backup (xml-publishing.mbz, Moodle 4.5.2, without user data); 36 extracted learning resources organised by module (learning-resources.zip: HTML pages with transcripts, 10 H5P interactive videos, 5 videos, 4 images, 1 PDF guideline); a file inventory with checksums (resource-inventory.csv); README.md with reuse guidance.

Instructional design: Karla Avanço, Marguerite Jan (OpenEdition). Review: Arnaud Gingold, Mohsine Aabid (OpenEdition).

All resources are available under CC BY 4.0. Questions, feedback and reuse reports: EDCH forum.

Modules

  1. Introduction to XML — theory and activity, 8 min (M. Kupreyev)
  2. XML for data visualisation — theory, 4 min (M. Kupreyev)
  3. XML for data exchange — theory and activity, 20 min (M. Kupreyev)
  4. XML for data quality — theory, 15 min (M. Kupreyev)
  5. Introduction to JATS XML — theory, 8 min (L. Jertec Musap)
  6. Preparing DOCX documents — tutorial, 10 min (L. Jertec Musap)
  7. JATS XML Converter Service — tutorial, 8 min (L. Jertec Musap)
  8. docxConverter plugin — tutorial, 3 min (D. Withanage)
  9. Texture plugin — tutorial, 5 min (D. Withanage)

Also: glossary, course map, feedback questionnaire aligned with the learning outcomes, further resources.

Technical information

Restoring the .mbz requires Moodle 4.5 or later and the plugins mod_questionnaire, enrol_autoenrol and block_vitrina. Pages use inline JavaScript, Bootstrap 4 accordions, Font Awesome icons and the Barlow font; visual equivalence on another site is not guaranteed. H5P packages can be imported into Moodle, WordPress, Drupal or Lumi. SHA-1 checksums of all extracted files are listed in resource-inventory.csv.
notes: Accessibility: transcripts for the videos of modules 1–5; written step-by-step instructions for the videos of module 6; no transcript for modules 7–9. Known issue: in module 6 ("Footnotes"), the video is not embedded in the HTML page; the file Footnotes.mp4 is included in the module folder. Alternative titles: XML Publishing; XML Publishing: Implementing XML in your publishing workflow.
